begrippen.definitie: Unique identification label for a physical storage medium (e.g. ARCHIVE-DISK-001). It is placed on a sticker on the medium and used as the directory name.
Physical sticker with the archive label, applied to the external medium so it can be recognized later without connecting it.
Mounting an external medium to the operating system in a way that makes writing impossible. Guarantees the original data remains unchanged.
Recursively traversing a medium and recording file properties (name, size, dates, document metadata) in the SQLite catalog.
The best available estimate of when a file's content was originally created, determined via a priority system (EXIF > document metadata > filename > filesystem).
Reliability indicator for original_content_date: high (document metadata), medium (filename), low (filesystem), suspect (unreliable).
Categorization of file extensions into functional groups: documenten, spreadsheets, databases, afbeeldingen, archieven, code_kennis.
Whether a file is currently accessible: online (medium connected), indexed_only (only metadata known), archive_offline (medium not connected), missing (expected but not found).
Intermediate saving of scan progress per directory, so an interrupted scan can be resumed later.
Full-text search index built by Recoll, stored separately per medium. Enables searching document content without having the medium connected.
Disk image backups made with the PING program (Partimage Is Not Ghost). Split into .000/.001/.002 files.
The process of connecting, registering, scanning, and indexing a new medium. The medium is 'ingested' into the workbench.

Technique to forward the USB port of another machine over the network (TCP port 3240) to the app host, so that a disk connected there appears on the app host as a local /dev/sdX and can be indexed normally.
The machine to which the disk is physically attached and that shares it via usbipd (bind). Windows: usbipd-win; Linux: usbip/usbipd.
The machine that mounts a shared USB disk over the network (usbip attach). Here always the app host (), which uses the vhci-hcd kernel module.
USB bus identification (e.g. 1-4 or 2-4) that designates a specific device on a host; used with usbip bind/attach.
Virtual USB host controller kernel module on the importer side; makes devices mounted over USB/IP appear as real USB devices.
